sample: The tracked file keeps 5,610 of the 155,866 stars the GALACTICNUCLEUS central catalogue lists within 6 arcminutes of Sgr A* brighter than Ks 16 (nuclear-cluster-sample.mts): those brighter than Ks 14, where the survey is as complete in the crowded centre as around it, and redder than H - Ks 1.3, the Galactic centre's own stars; inside two half-light radii of the cluster, on ellipses flattened 0.71 along the Galactic plane; each kept with the chance that it is the cluster's, one minus the star density of the 5 to 6 arcminute ring over that of its own half-arcminute ring (0.88 at the centre, 0.11 at the edge), drawn by its position; with a name from its position, RA, DEC and Ks.

around.basis: The cluster is centred on the black hole (Schödel et al. 2014, A&A 566, A47), so its stars are written around Sgr A*'s world origin, in parsecs: the S-stars on their orbits sit in the same frame.

frame.converter: Each sky position at a depth drawn from the spheroid's density along its sight line (frame.spheroid).

spheroid.basis: Gallego-Cano et al.'s (2020, A&A 634, A71; arXiv:2001.08182) Sérsic fit to the nuclear star cluster's star counts: effective radius 5.1 +/- 1.0 pc, index 2.2 +/- 0.7, axis ratio 0.71 +/- 0.10, flattened along the Galactic plane, so its axis points to Galactic north (position angle -58.6 degrees at Sgr A*). Centre and distance are Sgr A*'s (SIMBAD; GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, 8277 pc). The sample ends at two effective radii, and so does the spheroid. Each star's depth is drawn from it, not measured.

meaning: Stars of the Milky Way's nuclear star cluster around Sgr A*, from the GALACTICNUCLEUS survey (Nogueras-Lara et al. 2019, A&A 631, A20): one dot per star at its measured sky position, at a depth along the sight line drawn from the cluster's measured shape.

appearance.note: Presentation only: the app's catalogue star colour for B-V 1.2, a red giant's. The survey's own colours measure the dust in front of each star, not the star.

fullDetail.basis: Presentation choice: the cluster is whole within 100 pc of Sgr A*, ten times its reach; farther out it thins and then fades as it shrinks to a few pixels.

toneBy.band: Ks, as observed through the dust, at Sgr A*'s 8277 pc
toneBy.basis: Presentation choice: full tone at Ks 10 and brighter (absolute -4.6 at 8277 pc with no correction for dust), falling linearly in magnitude to 0.45 at the sample's Ks 14 limit, so the brightest giants stand out from the red clump.
